question: In a trapezoid, the two parallel sides are in the ratio 3:5. If the height of the trapezoid is 10 cm and its total area is 240 cm², determine the lengths of the parallel sides.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of parallel sides = (2 × Area) ÷ Height = (2 × 240) ÷ 10 = 48 cm.

Ratio of parallel sides = 3 : 5 (Total 8 parts).

Value of 1 part = 48 ÷ 8 = 6 cm.

Lengths are 3 × 6 = 18 cm and 5 × 6 = 30 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm and 30 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of parallel sides = 3 : 5

Height (h) = 10 cm

Total Area = 240 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Area of Trapezoid = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height

 

 
• 
 
 3x
 5x
 h = 10 cm
 Area = 240 cm²

⇒ Let the parallel sides be 3x and 5x.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (3x + 5x) × 10 = 240

⇒ 1/2 × 8x × 10 = 240

⇒ 40x = 240

⇒ x = 240 ÷ 40 = 6

⇒ Length of first parallel side = 3 × 6 = 18 cm

⇒ Length of second parallel side = 5 × 6 = 30 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm and 30 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Isosceles Trapezoid

A trapezoid in which the non-parallel sides are equal in length. The base angles are equal and the diagonals are of equal length.

Midsegment of a Trapezoid

The line connecting the midpoints of the non-parallel sides. Its length is the average of the two parallel sides: Midsegment = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Area of Parallelogram

Area = Base × Height. Opposite sides are equal and parallel, meaning a parallelogram is considered a special type of trapezoid.
